question.leadin: This country's 1991 breakup was followed by a series of namesake ethnic conflicts that lasted ten years.
question.text: Name this now-defunct socialist country that included the modern-day countries of Croatia, Montenegro, and Serbia.
question.answerHtml: Yugoslavia (accept Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia ; or SFRY )
question.clue: During World War II, this country's royalist government-in-exile signed the Treaty of Vis in a truce with the communist-leaning partisans.

swap.text: Princip carried out the assassination in this Bosnian city, its nation's capital.
swap.clue: Concrete scars left in this city were filled with red resin to make its namesake "roses."

question.leadin: A drone hovered over a soccer field with a flag of this country during a match, causing a fight between players from this country and Serbia.
question.text: Name this Balkan nation that, in 1998, backed the Kosovo Liberation Army in its bid for independence. In 2014, it was granted candidate status for EU membership.
question.clue: The primary language of this country is separated into the highland Gheg dialect and the lowland Tosk dialect.

swap.text: Princip also aligned himself with this secret Serbian military society, which had planted many would-be assassins throughout Sarajevo.
swap.clue: Organized in four or five member committees, its undisputed leader was a man known as "Apis," and its activities were enthusiastically supported for a time by Crown Prince Alexander.

question.text: The Ottomans fought this battle under the command of Murad I against the Serbs under Lazar. While both armies were wiped out, it led to a scarcity of Serbian troops, giving way to Serbian-Ottoman vassalage.
question.clue: Another source congratulates King Tvrtko I for success at this battle, which occurred on St. Vitus Day.

swap.text: In the March on Rome, Mussolini was aided by fascist militias wearing shirts of this color. This color also names an epidemic of bubonic plague in 14th century Europe and the Tuesday the American stock market crashed in 1929.
swap.clue: A Sioux medicine man was named after an elk of this color.

question.text: Tuđman's ("TOODJ-man") refusal to confirm opposition candidate Goran Granic as mayor of this capital of Croatia led to its namesake crisis, during which Tuđman compared protestors to "small-time cattle."
question.clue: The Maksimir Park and the Museum of Broken Relationships are both tourist attractions in this capital city of Croatia.

swap.text: This 1884 conference organized by the German Chancellor Otto von Bismarck regulated the rules of colonization and attempted to eliminate African autonomy and self-independence.
swap.clue: Another key participant here was Gyula Andrassy, who negotiated the occupation of Bosnia-Herzegovina by Austria-Hungary.

question.leadin: Given details of its twentieth century history, name the eastern European state.
question.text: Todor Zhivkov was the longtime Communist ruler of this country, which was one of the most lockstep allies of the USSR throughout the Cold War.
question.clue: One leader of this nation was ousted after members of the NGO Ecoglasnost were beaten by the police, leading to the one-year term of Petar Mladenov.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Ottoman incursions into Europe.
swap.text: Ottoman forces under Bayezid I routed Christian forces at the Battle of Nicopolis, which was fought at a fortress in this modern-day country. Basil II was known for slaying people of this country's namesake ethnicity.
swap.clue: The April Conspiracy targeted a leader of this country nicknamed "Bai Tosho."

question.leadin: This state emerged as an independent polity after its first ruler Basarab won the Battle of Posada.
question.text: Name this state, which later defended its independence from the Ottoman Empire at the Battle of Rovine under its ruler Mircea ("MEERCH-ya") the Great.

swap.text: Kostunica was president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia until March 2003, one month after the country adopted this new name. The country would keep this name until its two constituents broke apart in June 2006.

question.leadin: During the Log Revolution, people native to one of these two modern-day countries constructed blockades made of logs in the other, rejecting changes made after a 1990 election.
question.text: Name these two former members of Yugoslavia. Paramilitary units from one of them perpetrated the Vukovar Massacre in the other.
question.answerHtml: Serbia and Croatia [or Republic of Serbia and Republic of Croatia; accept Republika Hrvatska in place of “Croatia”; accept Republika Srbija in place of “Serbia”; do not accept answers mentioning “Republika Srpska,” because that’s different]

swap.text: The Nemanjic Dynasty ruled these people who name a modern country with capital at Belgrade.
swap.clue: This ethnicity venerates a member who pretended to defect in order to enter an enemy's camp and assassinate their ruler.

question.text: Greece was assigned to the Western sphere of influence in this agreement despite being mostly controlled by the EAM. Winston Churchill wrote down 2 numbers beside the names of five countries in his secret copy of this agreement.

swap.text: Because most fezzes were manufactured in the Austro-Hungarian Empire, the hat waned in popularity in 1908 during an Ottoman boycott of Austrian goods, which was launched in response to the Austrian annexation of this territory.

question.text: This failed 1944 action directed by Skorzeny was an attempt to kill Tito and end the resistance in Yugoslavia; partisan agents discovered the plot ahead of time and thwarted it.

swap.leadin: After killing Musa the Outlaw, whose chest contained three hearts and a snake, this rider of the piebald steed Sarac ("shah-RAHTS") was captured and nearly killed by Musa's even stronger brother, Djemo the Mountaineer.
swap.text: Name this Balkan hero with a "baby lamb"-sized mustache who sarcastically plowed Ottoman roads in one legend. In real life, this lord of Prilep succeeded his father Vukasin Mrnjavcevic ("vu-KAH-shin mern-YAHV-chuh-vits") in 1371 and built a namesake monastery near Skopje ("SCOP-yuh").

question.leadin: This time lasted from 1948 to 1954 and was named for the organization controlled by Stalin which Yugoslavia did not wish to join.
question.text: Identify this period, during which Yugoslavia's refusal to join the Warsaw Pact led to the constant threat of Soviets deposing the Yugoslavian leadership.
question.clue: This period during which over 100 citizens were killed at the Goli Otok ("GOH-lee OH-toke") prison camp. The Belgrade declaration ended this seven-year period with a rapprochement between the Soviet Union and another nation.

swap.leadin: An "old" faction led by Janez Bleiweis within this ethnic group clashed with a "young" faction in the second half of the 19th century over how radically to oppose Austrian rule.
swap.text: Name this ethnic group, the primary inhabitants of the Duchy of Carniola. Following WWI, they formed a namesake kingdom with Serbs and Croats.
swap.clue: In 1918, Peter I's kingdom expanded to form Yugoslavia, composed of Serbs, Croats, and this ethnic group. This ethnic group's namesake republic, which includes Melania Trump's birthplace in Novo Mesto, was the first country to break from Yugoslavia in 1990.
